answer.label: Attributed to
answer.authorDates: 1978–2020 · Los Angeles Lakers guard, five-time NBA champion
answer.sourceLine: Kobe Bryant really did say this, and there is a datable occasion for it: a press gathering on the Manila stop of Nike’s “Mamba Mentality Tour,” reported by two Philippine outlets on 25 June 2016. But neither contemporaneous transcription matches the sentence that circulates — both render it as two clauses, and neither contains the words “try to.” No transcript, recording or book page has been located carrying this exact wording.

source.heading: Where the line actually comes from

docMeta.dd: Philstar.com and Tiebreaker Times, same day

source.excerpt: It’s the constant quest to be the best version of yourself, the quest to be better today than yesterday.
trail: 25 June 2016 — Manila. Philstar.com ↗ reports Bryant, in town for Nike’s Mamba Mentality Tour, defining the phrase in a discussion with select media — his first trip since his final game the previous April.
Same day, second outlet. Tiebreaker Times ↗ covers the same Manila stop and transcribes the definition as two sentences, close to but not identical with Philstar’s version.
2020 — the version that spreads. Entertainment Tonight ↗ ties the fuller statement to the 2016 tour, hedged as “reportedly explained,” alongside his separate 2018 Amazon Book Review answers.

Undated — the sponsor’s wording. Nike’s Mamba Week ‘Fearless’ page ↗ prints the popular form, “It’s a constant quest to try to be better today than you were yesterday,” credited only to “Kobe Bryant on Mamba Mentality.”
source.excerptNote: That is Philstar.com’s wording. Tiebreaker Times, covering the same session, wrote it as two sentences: “It’s a constant quest to be the best version of yourself. It’s a quest to be better today than you were yesterday.” Neither contains “try to,” and neither opens with “The mamba mentality is.”

author.name: Kobe Bryant
author.heading: Kobe Bryant
author.bio: Kobe Bean Bryant was born in Philadelphia on 23 August 1978 and spent all twenty of his NBA seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers, winning five championships, the 2008 MVP award and two Olympic golds before retiring in April 2016 with a 60-point final game. He adopted the nickname Black Mamba mid-career and gradually built it into a public philosophy of relentless preparation, which he was still explaining on sponsor tours and in his 2018 book The Mamba Mentality: How I Play. He died in a helicopter crash in Calabasas, California on 26 January 2020, aged 41.

cite.sourceCitation: Olmin Leyba, “Kobe Bryant returns, preaches ‘Mamba Mentality’ to Filipinos,” Philstar.com, 25 June 2016; and JC Gonzales, “Kobe Bryant seeks to continue spreading Mamba Mentality,” Tiebreaker Times, 25 June 2016 — both reporting remarks made at the Manila stop of Nike’s Mamba Mentality Tour. Neither report carries the popular one-sentence wording.

copyAttribution: Kobe Bryant, remarks at the Manila stop of Nike's "Mamba Mentality Tour," reported 25 June 2016. As transcribed at the time: "It's the constant quest to be the best version of yourself, the quest to be better today than yesterday." The widely shared one-sentence version is a tightened paraphrase of that. Via Quotle.info

misattribution.heading: Right man, edited sentence
misattribution.intro: This is not a case of the wrong speaker. It is a case of a spoken answer being tidied into a single quotable sentence somewhere between 2016 and the meme graphics — and the tidying is visible if you line the versions up.

items.why: Neither same-day report contains “try to.” Philstar.com ↗ has “the quest to be better today than yesterday”; Tiebreaker Times ↗ has “It’s a quest to be better today than you were yesterday.”

items.who: One sentence opening “The mamba mentality is…”
items.why: As reported, Bryant gave two clauses — being the best version of yourself, then being better today than yesterday. Entertainment Tonight ↗ preserves the two-sentence shape; the circulating version collapses it and supplies the opening framing.

The two 25 June 2016 accounts do not agree word for word with each other, which is normal for extemporaneous remarks — and is why no single wording can be called the canonical text. Compare Philstar ↗ with Tiebreaker Times ↗.
The line does not appear on Wikiquote’s Kobe Bryant page ↗, and a search of Quote Investigator ↗ for “mamba mentality” returns nothing matched. No specialist has ruled on the wording either way.

misattribution.truthLine: He said it, and there is a date and a room: Manila, 25 June 2016, on the Manila stop of the Mamba Mentality Tour ↗. What travels is a smoothed-out version of what the reporters in that room wrote down.

context.heading: A retired man, still coaching
lead: In June 2016 Kobe Bryant had been retired for barely two months. Philstar.com noted that the Manila trip was his first since his final game the previous April — the 60-point night against Utah — and he had come as the face of a Nike tour built around a phrase he had coined for himself. Asked to define it, he did not reach for anything grand.

“I came up with it during one of our tours,” he said of the phrase, in the account Entertainment Tonight later collected ↗. “Because I put the kids through so many drills and clinics and I just thought to myself ‘mamba mentality.’” The definition that followed was deliberately small-scale, and the example he chose to illustrate it was not basketball at all.
context.detailsSummary: What he said about it afterwards
detailsBody: Two years later, promoting The Mamba Mentality: How I Play, Bryant gave a differently worded account to the Amazon Book Review: “Mamba mentality is all about focusing on the process and trusting in the hard work when it matters most.” He added that it “started just as a hashtag that came to me one day.” Both quotations are reproduced in Entertainment Tonight’s 2020 roundup ↗.

Nike itself still runs the tightened wording. Its “Mamba Week Day Four: Fearless” page ↗ prints “It’s a constant quest to try to be better today than you were yesterday,” credited simply to “Kobe Bryant on Mamba Mentality” — with no date, occasion or transcript given. Since Nike ran the 2016 tour, this is the closest thing to a corporate endorsement of the popular wording, but it is a marketing page, not a record.
context.pull: The other day at the house, my kids wanted me to make lasagna. When I make lasagna, it has to be the best lasagna I could possibly make; measure every detail of it.

sourcesVerified.claim: Philstar.com, dated 25 June 2016, reports Kobe Bryant in Manila for the Nike 'Mamba Mentality Tour' saying "It's the constant quest to be the best version of yourself, the quest to be better today than yesterday" — and notes it was his first trip since his final game the previous April; also carries the lasagna anecdote.

Tiebreaker Times, published 25 June 2016, covers the Manila stop of the Mamba Mentality Tour and quotes Bryant: "It's a constant quest to be the best version of yourself. It's a quest to be better today than you were yesterday."

Entertainment Tonight (24 Aug 2020) attributes to Bryant's 2016 Mamba Mentality Tour the statement "To sum up what mamba mentality is, it means to be able to constantly try to be the best version of yourself. That is what the mentality is. It's a constant quest to try to better today than you were yesterday," hedged as 'reportedly explained', and separately quotes his 2018 Amazon Book Review remarks including "Mamba mentality is all about focusing on the process and trusting in the hard work when it matters most" and "I came up with it during one of our tours."

Nike's 'Mamba Week Day Four: Fearless' page prints "It's a constant quest to try to be better today than you were yesterday." credited to 'Kobe Bryant on Mamba Mentality', with no date, occasion or source given.

Wikiquote's Kobe Bryant page does not list this quotation and has no Misattributed or Disputed section; it does carry sourced quotes from The Mamba Mentality: How I Play (2018) and his 13 April 2016 final-game speech.
A Quote Investigator site search for 'mamba mentality' returns 'Sorry, but nothing matched your search terms' — QI has no article on the phrase.

Wikipedia gives Kobe Bryant's birth date as 23 August 1978 (Philadelphia) and death as 26 January 2020 (Calabasas, aged 41), twenty seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers 1996–2016, five NBA championships, 2008 MVP, two Olympic gold medals.
